posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
Menu ext: (refer to the common event ID, so leave blank.
name should be in qoutes as given in my example (else it throws an error).
main bind and actor bind are different (read helpfile).
main bind starts directly, actor bind start after selecting an actor.
so if you call a SceneManager, you can leave out "menu ext" to be blank.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
I would suggest these YEP_MainMenuManager parameter values (untested):
Menu 2 Name
=
Yanfly.Param.ISSynthCmd
Menu 2 Symbol
=
synthesis
Menu 2 Show
=
$gameSystem.isShowSynthesis()
Menu 2 Enabled
=
$gameSystem.isEnableSynthesis()
Menu 2 Ext
= (nada)
Menu 2 Main Bind
=
SceneManager.push.bind(SceneManager, Scene_Synthesis)
Menu 2 Actor Bind
= (nada)
To change the command name, edit the
Command Name
parameter of YEP_ItemSynthesis.
Also, your Yanfly plugins are not in the recommended order, listed here:
Category:Yanfly Engine Plugins - Yanfly.moe Wiki
www.yanfly.moe
To avoid strange bugs, I suggest you click+drag to rearrange them into this order:
YEP_CoreEngine
YEP_MainMenuManager
YEP_ItemSynthesis
Save your project to apply Plugin Manager changes before testing!

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
From the
plugin's help
:
Plugin Command:
  OpenSynthesis          Opens up the Synthesis Scene from the field.
So you would use
Plugin Command
:
OpenSynthesis
in your common event.
Note that calling a common event will close the menu to run the event, which means:
There will probably be a flicker as it transfers from menu -> map -> crafting.
Closing the crafting menu will return you to the map, rather than the menu.
The alternative solution that I provided should skip the need for a common event completely~
Edit: I just realised something. You don't seem to be using YEP_MainMenuManager for anything else, so I recommend you turn it off or remove it.
Like Robro said earlier
, the Item Synthesis plugin should add its own command if its
Show Command
parameter is set to
true
. (By default YEP_MainMenuManager disables most menu commands from plugins.) The crafting command might not be placed exactly where you want it in the list, but it should certainly work.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Try this tag on the recipe book:
<Item Recipe: 1 to 6>
I.e. "when this item is in the inventory, you know how to craft items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6".
Spoiler:
source
Item, Weapon, and Armor Notetags:
  <Item Recipe: x>
  <Item Recipe: x, x, x>
  <Item Recipe: x to y>
  This will change this item into a recipe for x item(s). As long as this
  item is in possession by the party as a whole, item(s) x can be
  synthesized by the player provided that the player has the proper quantity
  of ingredients.
  * Note: Entries without names will not be included. Entries without both a
  synthesis cost and without an ingredient list will not be included.

  <Weapon Recipe: x>
  <Weapon Recipe: x, x, x>
  <Weapon Recipe: x to y>
  This will change this item into a recipe for x weapon(s). As long as this
  item is in possession by the party as a whole, weapon(s) x can be
  synthesized by the player provided that the player has the proper quantity
  of ingredients.
  * Note: Entries without names will not be included. Entries without both a
  synthesis cost and without an ingredient list will not be included.

  <Armor Recipe: x>
  <Armor Recipe: x, x, x>
  <Armor Recipe: x to y>
  This will change this item into a recipe for x armor(s). As long as this
  item is in possession by the party as a whole, armor(s) x can be
  synthesized by the player provided that the player has the proper quantity
  of ingredients.
  * Note: Entries without names will not be included. Entries without both a
  synthesis cost and without an ingredient list will not be included.
Then put this kind of tag on each craftable item:
<Synthesis Ingredients>
item 4: 2
item 5
</Synthesis Ingredients>
I.e. "craft this item using 2 of item ID 4, and 1 of item ID 5".
Spoiler:
source
<Synthesis Ingredients>
    item id
    item id: x
    weapon id
    weapon id: x
    armor id
    armor id: x
    gold: x
    named item
    named item: x
  </Synthesis Ingredients>
  Using the above tag in an item will set those items as the ingredients
  required for the player to synthesize. Replace "id" with the proper item,
  weapon, or armor ID's. If no ":x" is used, the database will register that
  as only needing 1 of that item as an ingredient. If "gold: x" is used,
  that will be the cost required to synthesize the item.

  If you are using named entries, priority will be given to the highest ID
  in the order of items, weapons, then armors.

  * Note: If you are using Item Core, Independent Items cannot become an
  ingredient for a recipe and will therefore be automatically omitted.
You can usually find full instructions for a plugin in its Help section. For example, the information in these "source" spoilers is from there. A plugin's help can be found in the scrollable box on the left side of the Plugin Manager:
Different plugins do things differently: you always need to read the manual.

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
remove the "null" from actor bind (just leave blank here).
plugin command or scriptcall in the common event (6) can be left blank
if you use "Main Bind", so the common event doesn't run.
the Ext only runs if you use the common event scriptcall inside the main bind.
plugin command should be:
OpenSynthesis
as for the
scriptcall:
SceneManager.push(Scene_ItemSynthesis)
.
Plugin Commands and Scriptcalls are 2 different things.
Ext that target the common event would the Main Bind to be:
this.callCommonEvent.bind(this)
.
read the helpfile what they exactly do, or check the video carefully.
scriptcall and/or plugin commands can be used to interact on items on the map
to open this window.
even items in your inventory to open them through common event.
